# Mississippi River Map Skills Lesson Plan
Foxglove Middle School | Grade 7 | 03/18/2026 | 10:00–10:45 a.m.

## Lesson overview
Teacher: Isabel Duarte | Class: 7B | 28 students
Objective: Students will use a map scale to estimate distances along the Mississippi River and identify three states the river borders.
Materials: Projected U.S. map, student river maps, rulers, pencils, and exit slips.

## Instructional sequence
- 10:00–10:05: Ask students to name a river they have seen on a map; record responses on the board.
- 10:05–10:15: Demonstrate how to measure a route with a ruler and convert map inches to miles. The student map key states that 1 inch represents 50 miles.
- 10:15–10:24: In pairs, students locate the Mississippi River, measure one segment, and compare estimates. Circulate and ask pairs to explain their conversions.
- 10:24–10:38: Students plot the river's route on graph paper individually. The map scale is 1 inch = 100 miles, so a 3-inch segment represents 300 miles.
- 10:38–10:43: Review answers aloud. Students name three states bordering the river and explain one measurement.
- 10:43–10:45: Collect exit slips with each student's route estimate and state list.

## Checks and follow-up
During pair work, note which students correctly multiply measured inches by 50. Use the exit slips to group students for the next lesson's map-scale warm-up. Neil Petrov will collect the student maps after class. Frank Hendricks will receive the lesson notes for the grade-level planning folder.
